title: Conditional Sentences — Types 0, 1, 2, 3 and Inversions
description: Condition aur result clauses ki syntax, Types 0, 1, 2, 3 ke structural formulas, mixed conditionals, inverted structures (Had I..., Were he...), aur competitive exam traps ko master karein.
learningObjectives: Condition clause (if-clause) aur result clause ke syntactic function aur clause ordering ko identify karein
Chaar standard conditional types (Types 0, 1, 2, aur 3) ke meaning aur verb formulas ko master karein
Factual truths, realistic future, hypothetical present, aur unreal past conditions mein accurately distinguish karein
Contextual time references ke hisaab se mixed conditionals ko analyze aur construct karein
Formal English aur exam questions mein aane wali conditional inversions (Had, Were, Should) ko master karein
Unless, provided that, as long as jaise conditional connectives ke rules aur limitations ko apply karein
High Court exams ke recurring formula traps (jaise if-clause mein 'would' ya 'will' ka use) ko eliminate karein

included: Condition clause (if-clause) vs main/result clause syntax aur comma rules
Zero Conditional (Type 0): General facts, scientific laws, aur recurring cause-and-effect
First Conditional (Type 1): Realistic future conditions aur modal/imperative variations
Second Conditional (Type 2): Hypothetical/unlikely present ya future situations aur subjunctive 'were'
Third Conditional (Type 3): Unreal counterfactual past conditions aur imagined past results
Mixed Conditionals: Past condition with present result, aur continuing state with past result
Conditional Inversions: 'Had + S + V3', 'Were + S + to + V1 / adjective', 'Should + S + V1'
Related Conjunctions: 'Unless' (if... not), 'provided that', 'as long as', 'in case'
High Court exam ke recurring distractors aur formula errors ka elimination
excluded: Voice: Active & Passive Voice transformations across tenses (Lesson 04 & 05 mein covered hain)
Narration: Direct & Indirect speech reporting changes (Lesson 06 & 07 mein covered hain)
General non-conditional conjunctions (Lesson 14 Connectives mein covered hain)
Standard non-conditional Subject-Verb Agreement rules (Lesson 13 mein covered hain)
